name: JWT expired token accepted
description:
The application accepts a JSON Web Token whose exp (expiration time) claim is in the past. The signature is verified, but the expiry is not enforced, so a token that leaked once (from a log, a browser, a proxy) works for as long as its signing key does, and logging out or a short token lifetime protects nothing.

burpsy reports this only by differential: either the captured token's own exp is in the past and it is still accepted while the same token with an altered signature is refused, or the token's HMAC secret is a wordlist entry, the original claims re-signed by burpsy are accepted, and the same claims re-signed with exp a day in the past are accepted too, twice.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for it.
remediation: Validate exp (and nbf) on every request, with at most a small clock-skew allowance, and reject tokens without an exp where the token is a session credential. Use a maintained JWT library with claim validation switched on.

references.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy: JWT attacks
